title: Pulse Formula Recognition: How Mathematical Content Extraction Works
summary: Pulse's formula recognition converts mathematical content directly into machine-readable LaTeX. | Pulse AI
body_text: Introduction Mathematical formulas represent one of the most challenging frontiers in document extraction. While standard OCR excels at linear text and language character recognition, mathematical notation introduces spatial complexity that breaks traditional character-by-character approaches. Today, we're excited to announce Pulse's Formula Recognition submodule, a specialized component of our extraction pipeline designed specifically for mathematical content. The Mathematical Content Challenge Mathematical notation is fundamentally different from natural language text. Consider the expression: \[ \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2} + \lambda \nabla^2 f = 0 \] ‍ Traditional OCR might see this as a sequence of disconnected symbols: ∂, ², f, /, ∂, x, ², etc. But mathematically, this represents a differential equation where symbol positioning, superscripts, subscripts, and operator precedence carry semantic meaning. The challenge becomes exponentially more complex with: Handwritten papers with inconsistent spacing Complex fractions with nested denominators Matrix notation with precise alignment requirements Multi-line equations with continuation symbols Mixed mathematical and textual content in research papers and academia settings ‍ Source document (Abbott’s Real Analysis) Pulse Bounding Box Step Pulse Markdown/LaTeX Rendered Output ‍ Our Approach: Specialized Vision Architecture Rather than forcing mathematical content through general-purpose models, we developed a dedicated mini-model within the Pulse pipeline specifically for formula recognition. This approach allows us to: 1. Mathematical Symbol Understanding Our vision encoder is trained to recognize mathematical symbols as semantic units rather than simple character patterns. The model understands that ∫ is an integral operator requiring specific bounds notation, that Σ implies summation with index variables, and that parentheses in mathematical contexts have precedence implications. The translation into LaTeX syntax is done as a post step. 2. Spatial Relationship Modeling Mathematical notation relies heavily on spatial positioning. Our model processes formulas as 2D structures, understanding that: Superscripts indicate exponents or indices Subscripts denote variables or tensor notation Fraction bars create hierarchical groupings Radical symbols encompass expressions beneath them The vision encoder uses attention mechanisms specifically tuned for these spatial relationships, allowing it to correctly interpret complex nested structures. 3. Context-Aware LaTeX Generation Our output layer generates clean, compilable LaTeX code that preserves both the visual appearance and semantic meaning of the original formula. The model has been trained to: Choose appropriate LaTeX commands for specific mathematical contexts Handle edge cases in notation (e.g., distinguishing between multiplication and cross products) Maintain proper grouping and operator precedence Generate readable LaTeX that human reviewers can easily verify ‍ Source Document (CMU class notes) Pulse Bounding Box Step Pulse Markdown/LaTeX Rendered Output Training Data and Methodology Dataset Construction As is often the case with such specialized, fine-tuned models, data is the bottleneck. We assembled a training/test corpus of 10M+ formula/LaTeX pairs from diverse sources: Academic Papers : Mathematical journals, physics preprints, engineering specifications Handwritten Content : Student notebooks, professor lecture notes, research sketches Technical Documentation : Standards documents, patent filings, regulatory submissions Historical Sources : Scanned mathematical texts, archived research papers Ground Truth Generation Creating accurate LaTeX ground truth at scale required a multi-stage verification process, and we worked with many academic labs, researchers, and offshore data labeling teams to make this possible. Our steps included: Initial LaTeX compilation verification to ensure syntactic correctness Visual rendering comparison between source and generated LaTeX Human expert review for mathematical accuracy and semantic preservation Cross-validation against multiple LaTeX compilers (pdfTeX, XeTeX, LuaTeX) for robustness Technical Performance Accuracy Metrics It’s incredibly important to build a robust eval pipeline to continuously improve the model on. We’ll give a high-level overview here of this stage, but we have a dedicated open-source benchmark with code snippets in the works to be released soon! We evaluate formula recognition using multiple metrics that capture different aspects of mathematical content extraction: Symbol-Level Accuracy : Character-by-character comparison of mathematical symbols Structure Preservation : Hierarchical matching of mathematical expressions LaTeX Compilation Rate : Percentage of outputs that compile without errors Semantic Equivalence : Mathematical meaning preservation across different valid LaTeX representations We tested the mathematical expressions in documents across resolution ranges, with artificial noise, skew, and rotations incorporated to evaluate performance variability. Real-World Applications Academic Research Workflows AI teams and academic labs are already using Pulse's formula recognition for: Literature Review Automation : Extracting mathematical models from research papers for systematic comparison Knowledge Base Construction : Building searchable databases of mathematical techniques and formulas Research Acceleration : Converting handwritten research notes into digital, searchable formats ‍ Performance at Scale To date, we have processed over 700 million pages through the Pulse pipeline. Mathematical content appears in approximately 15% of academic documents and 8% of technical enterprise documents in our corpus across all customers. Our formula recognition submodule has maintained: 99.2% uptime across production deployments <100ms average latency per formula recognition operation 94% first-pass accuracy on complex mathematical expressions 98.7% LaTeX compilation success rate for generated outputs ‍ Looking Forward Mathematical content extraction represents just one dimension of the specialized model approach we're taking with Pulse. We're actively improving and researching similar submodules for: Circuit diagram parsing for electrical engineering specifications and patent documents Table extraction and structure recognition for complex financial and regulatory filings Chart and graph vision extraction for automatic data digitization from research publications ‍ Get Early Access We're offering early access to Pulse's Formula Recognition submodule for AI teams, academic labs, and enterprise users working with mathematical content. The response from research institutions has been exceptional - our specialized approach consistently outperforms general OCR solutions on mathematical content by significant margins. Interested in testing formula recognition with your mathematical content? Contact our team for a demonstration and early access to the submodule. -- The Pulse team continues to push the boundaries of document extraction accuracy. Our specialized model approach allows us to tackle domain-specific challenges that general-purpose solutions leave unsolved. Formula recognition is just the beginning.

title: IPG Photonics Receives Order From Lockheed Martin for CROSSBOW™ High-Energy Laser Systems

This follow-on order from Lockheed Martin reflects both the clear demand for deployable directed energy solutions and the readiness of our product,” said Dr. Mark Gitin, Chief Executive Officer of IPG Photonics. title: EnerSys® Announces Incremental Benefits From IRA Section 45X Tax Credits and Increases Adjusted Diluted Earnings Per Share Guidance
summary: EnerSys® Announces Incremental Benefits From IRA Section 45X Tax Credits and Increases Adjusted Diluted Earnings Per Share Guidance
body_text: EnerSys® Announces Incremental Benefits From IRA Section 45X Tax Credits and Increases Adjusted Diluted Earnings Per Share Guidance READING, Pa., Dec. 17, 2024 (BUSINESS WIRE) - EnerSys (NYSE: ENS), a global leader in stored energy solutions for industrial applications, today announced incremental benefits associated with the Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit, part of Section 45X of the Internal Revenue Code (IRC). Based on final regulations for certain direct material input costs recently issued by the U.S. Treasury Department, and subsequent review by EnerSys’ external advisors, the Company has refined its calculations to expand the value of its benefits for tax credits, including credits related to its production of Electrode Active Material. EnerSys estimates the incremental benefits to be approximately $3 million to $4 million per quarter. As a result, EnerSys will record a one-time catch-up adjustment during its fiscal third quarter 2025 of $30 million to $35 million to reflect benefits retroactive to its fiscal fourth quarter of 2023, when the Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit under IRC 45X originally took effect. As a result of the incremental benefits, EnerSys is raising its fiscal third quarter 2025 and full year fiscal 2025 adjusted diluted earnings per share (EPS) guidance ranges to incorporate these benefits. The Company had previously provided third quarter adjusted diluted EPS guidance in the range of $2.20 to $2.30 and full year adjusted diluted EPS guidance between $8.75 and $9.05. With the incremental Section 45X benefits, EnerSys now anticipates third quarter fiscal 2025 adjusted diluted EPS of $3.00 to $3.10 and full year fiscal 2025 adjusted diluted EPS of $9.65 to $9.95. Based on the final regulations, the Company expects to record annual tax credits as a reduction to cost of goods sold and not subject to taxation to be in the range of approximately $135 million to $175 million. This compares to the previously communicated annual range of approximately $120 million to $160 million. The Company expects to continue to receive tax credits associated with its qualifying U.S. production volumes through December 31, 2032. click here to view the full press release

title: ICON portfolio of AI tools drives clinical trial efficiencies
body_text: Dublin, Ireland – 30 January 2025 – ICON plc , (NASDAQ: ICLR) a world-leading clinical research organisation powered by healthcare intelligence, today announced the expansion of its portfolio of artificial intelligence (AI) tools that deliver efficiencies across the clinical trial process, including study startup, document management, resource forecasting and metrics reporting. ICON has invested significantly in its AI and digital capabilities through the establishment of its AI Centre of Excellence. The centre, which comprises a dedicated team of data scientists, engineers and domain experts, is responsible for developing and deploying AI solutions that accelerate trials, enhance data and optimise operational efficiencies. The centre is supported by an AI Governance Committee, which oversees ethical, legal and data privacy standards in the deployment of new solutions. The latest solutions to be launched are: iSubmit, which automates the clinical trial document management process. It uses AI to improve compliance, reduce the burden on clinical project teams, and manage documents in an efficient and accurate way based on defined rules. Mapi Research Trust COA leverages AI to remain current with latest Clinical Outcome Assessments (COAs) from public sources in near real-time. It provides comprehensive intelligence to support optimal clinical trial protocols/designs. FORWARD+ is an AI-enabled capability that provides industry-leading visibility into resource demands, allocations and forecasting. FORWARD+ ensures efficient resource management through the clinical trial process. Study Start-up Site Contracts is an AI-enabled capability that streamlines the clinical contract drafting process by leveraging historical clinical contracts in order to create comprehensive near final draft contracts. OMR AI Navigation Assistant empowers operational clinical study metrics with generative AI to provide industry-leading analytics to transform data into business insights. Based on its success to date in implementing innovative AI solutions for its customers, ICON plans to further enhance its award-winning capabilities in how AI can drive productivity and efficiencies in clinical trials, with support from Enterprise Ireland. This sustained focus on investment in AI solutions by ICON will support its customers as they look to overcome some of the challenges in realising the potential of AI in drug development. A recent ICON survey of biopharma companies found that 13% of respondents indicated that while AI and digital technologies are being heavily used in single development programs, it is challenging for organisations to systemically incorporate them, possibly due to the complexity of managing such strategic, enterprise-scale digital disruption. Tom O’Leary, CIO at ICON, commented: “Our research indicates that while the potential of AI to transform the drug development process is widely acknowledged, realising this potential at scale will take time and investment. As a leading clinical research organisation, it is our role to innovate the clinical trial process to support our customers in delivering new medicines to patients faster. We’re pleased to launch these additional new solutions, developed in a responsible and comprehensive way, which will deliver faster, smarter and more reliable outcomes for our customers.” Leo Clancy, CEO, Enterprise Ireland, commented: “Enterprise Ireland is delighted to support ICON in advancing its AI capabilities, which are driving significant innovation in the clinical trial process. By investing in cutting-edge technologies, ICON is not only enhancing efficiency and compliance but also accelerating the development of life-saving treatments. This partnership exemplifies how Irish companies are leading the way in leveraging AI to address global challenges in healthcare and deliver meaningful impact for patients worldwide.” ICON’s latest AI solutions complement its existing multi-award-winning AI tools. These include One Search , which enables access to multiple data sources and provides the visualisation and tools necessary for optimum site identification, based on ICON and industry data of site capability, experience and performance. ICONex maps out global networks of key opinion leaders across therapeutic areas, reducing the time it takes to identify the most influential experts for clinical trials from weeks to minutes. Cassandra predicts post-marketing study requirements early, allowing for proactive planning and reducing the risk of regulatory delays. For further information please visit: www.iconplc.com/ai . About ICON plc ICON plc is a world-leading healthcare intelligence and clinical research organisation. From molecule to medicine, we advance clinical research providing outsourced services to pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device and government and public health organisations. We develop new innovations, drive emerging therapies forward and improve patient lives. With headquarters in Dublin, Ireland, ICON employed approximately 42,250 employees in 106 locations in 55 countries as at September 30, 2024. For further information about ICON, visit: www.iconplc.com. Media contacts: Claire Quinn, Corporate Communications, ICON +353 87 4066091 claire.quinn@iconplc.com Lisa Henry, Weber Shandwick (PR adviser) +44 7785 458203 lhenry@webershandwick.com ICON/ICLR-G

title: Email checklist before sending: 7 steps to catch errors
summary: Run this 7-step pre-send email checklist to catch bad segments, deliverability gaps, and broken links before they cost you revenue and trigger unsubscribes.
body_text: Shift to autonomous marketing Generated by Klaviyo AI The post explains how Klaviyo’s Marketing Agent moves teams from manual campaign execution toward more autonomous, strategy-focused marketing. It outlines how unified customer data, practical use cases, and built-in guardrails enable brands to generate, refine, and govern AI-driven campaigns without sacrificing control. From manual to autonomous: Marketing Agent reduces operational work like building campaigns step by step so marketers can focus more on lifecycle strategy and customer experience. Unified data foundation: Klaviyo’s built-in CDP unifies customer, product, and engagement data so Marketing Agent can generate relevant ideas, audiences, and channel recommendations with full context. Practical use cases: Brands use Marketing Agent to accelerate onboarding, maintain an educational campaign calendar, and act as a strategy engine for larger teams during planning and optimization. Guardrails and control: Brand voice analysis, fact-based content generation, promotion accuracy checks, and compliance safeguards help keep AI-generated campaigns on-brand and compliant. More time for strategy: By taking on repetitive implementation tasks, Marketing Agent frees retention teams to identify new lifecycle moments, refine segmentation, and focus on growth-driving work. Sign up Get a demo The most effective way to prevent mistakes in your emails is actually fairly boring: it’s a checklist. All marketers, even the most tenured, can benefit from a comprehensive checklist before launching a new campaign or automation. Here, we’ve broken down a main checklist into 7 mini checklists that can help you prevent mistakes and maximize revenue for every email you send. Depending on the size of your list and the number of ways you personalize your emails, you may want to rely more on one checklist over another. 1. Performance goals: You’re set up for success According to Klaviyo’s 2026 email benchmarks , email campaigns see an average click rate of 1.69% while flows see an average of 5.58%. Automated messages consistently deliver 6–8x more revenue per send vs. campaigns. That being said, your industry average may be different from the overall average. When you’re deciding on performance goals, it’s important to get a good sense of what success looks like in your industry for click rate, conversion rate, revenue per email, and unsubscribe rate. Once you’ve aligned on these goals with your leadership team, establish tracking and attribution mechanisms. Omnichannel, linear multi-touch attribution spreads the credit evenly across all meaningful touchpoints, but you’ll need to decide how you want to customize your model to consider the credit granted to your email campaigns and flows. The important thing to remember is that this approach to attribution hinges on the concept that real-life buying journeys don’t follow a straight line. A customer might first discover your brand via an ad, browse your products on mobile, click through an email campaign later, get a cart reminder via text message, and finally make a purchase on desktop. To achieve a holistic sense of attribution, you’ll need to implement UTM parameters in all your emails. These are short text tags added to the end of a URL, so your site analytics can track email performance by campaign and content block, such as your hero banner vs. your final CTA. Finally, make sure your email campaigns and flows follow a standardized naming convention format in your marketing automation platform . This is so that your campaigns and flows are searchable by your entire team, and so that your reports are easy to generate and interpret. Performance goal checklist: Email performance benchmark review KPI alignment with leadership Attribution model customization UTMs and tracking codes Standardized naming conventions 2. Deliverability: Your emails are making it into primary inboxes Before sending any email, you’ll need to signal to email clients that you’re a legitimate sender. This requires setting up infrastructure in your marketing automation platform to signal that it’s allowed to send on your behalf and that nobody is forging your domain. Specifically, this means setting up: Sender Policy Framework (SPF): This record lists the servers allowed to send email on behalf of your domain, so mailbox providers can confirm a message really came from you. DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM): This signature is added to every message so the receiving server can verify the email wasn't altered in transit. Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC): This policy tells mailbox providers what to do with messages that fail SPF or DKIM, and reports back on who is using your domain to send mail. You’ll also want to run a placement test. A test can tell you whether you're landing in people’s primary inbox or in promotions or spam. It also flags spammy phrasing or a bad link before your real list ever sees it. If your reputation has taken a hit, check whether your domain or IP has turned up on a public block list, which can throttle your delivery until you sort it out. Finally, make sure you’ve implemented a one-click unsubscribe link with the necessary infrastructure to automatically remove recipients from your list. Not only is this required by regulations, but it also prevents recipients from flagging your email as spam, which can ultimately drag down your sender reputation and damage deliverability. Deliverability checklist: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC set-up Successful placement test Check public block lists (if you can’t achieve a successful placement test) One-click unsubscribe 3. Segmentation: The right people are getting the right emails According to Klaviyo’s Future of Consumer Marketing Report , 74% of shoppers expect personalized experiences from brands. Granular segmentation is the precursor to personalization. Every single email campaign and flow should be using audience segmentation to make sure your messages are relevant to recipients. That means targeting shoppers based on: Behavior: purchases, browsing, channel preferences, etc. Preferences: quiz results, anniversaries, lifestyle, etc. Predictive analytics : churn risk, customer lifetime value (LTV), average order value (AOV), etc. Before sending, determine exactly who is most likely to respond to the offer. For example, if the goal is to make VIPs feel special with an early access offer, figure out which VIPs are most likely to engage. Maybe you want to break it down by browsing behavior, AOV, or quiz result. If you want to speed up this process, an AI marketing agent can build out your segments from scratch or find the right segment for your message. AI can also optimize that audience further by automatically suppressing who’s most likely to unsubscribe, so you can protect deliverability. Segmentation checklist: Behavioral, preference, and/or predictive audience segmentation Larger audience segment breakdown With AI: audience segment creation With AI: automatic suppression of likely unsubscribers 4. Copy: There’s a clear reason to buy for each segment Your copy should follow the segment you want to reach. A first-time subscriber and a loyal customer should receive different messages. Tailor copy to the shopper’s lifecycle stage, based on what they browsed, bought, or skipped. When creating your email copy, you’ll also want to lead with a benefit that’s relevant to that audience segment. Open with what the reader can expect from your offer, so the value is clear in the first line and the preview text. Your subject line should also orient toward the same promise. Pull in dynamic, personalized content to boost the likelihood of engagement. That means using personalized blocks like AI product recommendations drawn from real customer data housed in a CRM. When your product recommendations reflect real purchase and browsing data, they’re much more likely to land. Finally, make sure you’re using only one call-to-action button. This is to make sure your email has a clear next step, so recipients can easily jump on the offer you want them to convert on. Tip: Use an AI marketing agent to speed up the production process. With plain-text prompts, marketers can direct AI to draft the email, write follow-up messages, and stage timing. Copy checklist: Segment-offer alignment Subject line-offer alignment Benefit-led opener and preview text Dynamic blocks of personalized content One clear CTA With AI: copy production with prompting 5. Accessibility: Everyone can read and understand your emails An accessible email is one that reaches more people, including people with disabilities and without. By default, every email should come with the option to view as plain-text only for screen readers and those who choose not to view images in their emails. Background and text color should have sufficient contrast for people with visual impairments, and every image should come with alt text for screen readers. Accessibility runs deeper than alt text, though. Screen readers move through your email by its structure, so use real heading hierarchy rather than simply bold text. Also, make sure your text is large enough for people with low vision to read: the recommendation is a font size of 14 pt or larger. Accessibility checklist: Plain-text version Screen reader test pass Dark mode legibility Alt text for all images High color contrast between background and text color Sufficient white space 14 pt or larger font size No image-only design 6. Frequency and timing: You’re sending emails at the right time Before you send an email campaign, make sure it’s not doubling up on the work of your automations. Automations are triggered by customer behavior, such as abandoning a cart or even a lack of engagement over a certain period of time. Those automations do a lot of work behind the scenes to generate revenue: as previously mentioned, they deliver 6–8x more revenue per send vs. campaigns, according to Klaviyo’s 2026 benchmarks. This is why it’s important to let automations do their job rather than sending an email campaign that’s too similar. To keep unsubscribe rates low, rely on email campaigns for more time-sensitive communication, such as news, events, and seasonal moments. You’ll also want to make sure your emails are sent at optimal times, too. With AI, your CRM can predict when each recipient is most likely to open, click, and convert across channels. Personalized send time replaces batch sending with AI models that can send emails at the optimal time for each customer based on past behavior and similar profiles. Frequency and timing checklist: Unique email campaign content compared to automations With AI: personalized send time 7. Omnichannel messages: You’re sending on the right channel to begin with To build an email strategy that complements text messaging, you can use AI to choose the right channel for each person. AI that’s embedded within your CRM can draw from customer data to determine where someone is most likely to engage. Let’s say someone has been ignoring your text messages for a few months but has engaged consistently via email. AI channel affinity would automatically route an email to that customer, then switch up the strategy if that same customer decided to start engaging with text messages again. When email, text messages, and other touchpoints read from one shared, real-time profile, AI can sequence a customer's experience across channels instead of blasting each one in isolation. This reduces message fatigue and increases the likelihood of conversion. Omnichannel messages checklist: With AI: engagement-based email campaigns and flows With AI: engagement-based text message campaigns and flows Send more personalized emails with Klaviyo Composer Checklists are important for avoiding email marketing mistakes, but Composer , Klaviyo’s AI marketing agent, can reveal the revenue opportunities you may be missing. With plain-text prompts, marketers can ask where customers are dropping off and how they can make their email campaigns and flows better. Composer analyzes the sequence end-to-end, surfaces which step is underperforming and why, and recommends fixes in plain language. From there, marketers can use a single prompt to build a complete campaign: audience, copy, channel coordination, timing, all in one conversational session. title: Lyft Names Senthil Padmanabhan as CTO
summary: With decades of leadership at eBay, Senthil brings the technical depth & leadership range to help Lyft lead the industry in customer-obsessed AI.
body_text: Lyft is welcoming Senthil Padmanabhan as Chief Technology Officer, joining July 20, 2026, reporting to CEO David Risher. With decades of experience, Senthil is the rare technical leader who operates at every altitude: going deep on the most complex problems, driving company-wide change at a global scale, and bringing the team with him every step of the way. Most recently as VP of Engineering at eBay, where he first earned recognition as a Technical Fellow, Senthil scaled the company's core engineering platform, applications and infrastructure. His leadership helped eBay become the segment leader in key categories such as Parts & Accessories and Collectibles, while making eBay the fastest e-commerce site globally. He led a company-wide AI transformation that fundamentally changed what his teams could build, enhancing customer experiences and dramatically increasing engineering throughput – and transformed how those teams work, reducing deployment cycle times which has resulted in 10x more deployments and 6x more experiments than was possible four years ago. In a moment where companies are often tempted to use AI only to cut costs, Lyft is betting differently on what it can unlock: faster innovations and experiences for riders and drivers that weren't possible before. At Lyft, Senthil will lead the engineering foundations that power everything the company builds – and in an era where AI is reshaping how we work, those foundations matter more than ever. Senthil will set that direction: building on a world-class technical foundation to unlock what the company is able to deliver – helping riders get where they need to go, supporting the drivers who make that possible, and connecting people to the places and communities that matter to them. “Lyft has a clear purpose, a product millions of people love and rely on every day, and a team that genuinely cares about getting it right,” said Senthil. "My job is to make sure the Lyft ceiling keeps rising – using technology to multiply what we can achieve and unlock what wasn't possible before." Outside of work, Senthil is an avid reader and self-described foodie who loves exploring new restaurants with his sons. He and his wife are longtime Lyft riders who swear by scheduled rides to the airport. His tip: book the night before, and the rest takes care of itself.
